findings: All acceptance cases appear correctly handled by the implementation logic.
typeof boolean check correctly rejects true/false since typeof true === 'boolean', not 'number'.
typeof null check correctly rejects null since typeof null === 'object', not 'number'.
String rejection works correctly via typeof check.
Negative amount throws via amount < 0 check.
Zero or negative servings throw via <= 0 checks.
Underflow case (5e-324 with ratio 0.5) throws via amount > 0 && result === 0 check.
Ratio overflow/underflow edge cases (1e-308/1e308 or 1e308/1e-308) correctly produce non-finite or zero ratio, triggering throws.
No imports, side effects, external resources, or forbidden capabilities present; function is pure and self-contained.

summary: Implements scaleLinearAmount as a pure TypeScript function with strict validation. Checks that all three arguments are typeof 'number' (rejecting booleans, null, strings), all are finite, amount>=0, both servings>0. Computes ratio=targetServings/originalServings, throws if ratio is non-finite or zero. Computes result=amount*ratio, throws if result is non-finite or if a positive amount underflows to zero. Returns result with no rounding, preserving tiny quantities; zero amount returns zero when ratio is valid.
